headline: Shift Data Center Grid Costs
short_summary: This bill aims to make large energy users, such as data centers, responsible for their own grid infrastructure costs, rather than socializing them across all ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, Governor Spanberger's administration, U.S. Sen. Mark Warner, Delegate John McAuliff.
opponents: Data center industry, Data Center Coalition.
news_headline: Virginia bill aims to cut residential energy costs by shifting expenses to data centers
news_summary: A Virginia bill seeks to shift energy costs to data centers, potentially saving residential customers over $65 annually. If passed, data center costs would increase by roughly 16%, while residential rates could drop from 3.5% to 3%.

headline: Mandate Data Center Water Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates data centers to report their water consumption, providing transparency on their environmental impact and aiding water resource management.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Virginia League of Conservation Voters, Potomac Conservancy, environmental groups, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
news_headline: New law requires data center water usage reporting
news_summary: This legislation mandates water suppliers to report the volume of water provided to data centers, giving Virginia DEQ crucial information for water resource management. The bill was signed into law, providing a new tool to protect water supplies and hold the industry accountable.

headline: Regulate Data Center Siting, Noise
short_summary: This bill requires site assessments for new large data centers, including noise profiles and potential impacts on local resources, empowering localities in their approval processes.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental groups, Delegate Joshua E. Thomas, Delegate Sam Rasoul.
news_headline: Virginia bill mandates data center site assessments
news_summary: This bill requires Virginia localities to mandate site assessments for new data centers over 100 MW, examining noise impacts on nearby homes and schools. Localities can also request reviews on water, agriculture, parks, historic sites, and forests to inform approval decisions.
